page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top above the text, with page number 4. Two headings: "Exercitatio II." and the subtitle beneath it, both centred. Catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: Obiect. III. Non solus Cicero, Cæsar, &c. scripserunt latinè:
Resp. Sed hi purissimè. Magis igitur imitan-di.

Resp. I. Multi videntur corrupti, qui non sunt. II. Corrupta corrigantur, judicio, ex probatis authoritatibus: ab iis, qui possunt: non adolescentum temeritate vel conjecturis, quibus magis depravantur & dubii redduntur boni authores.
(Conclusio breviter commendet studium purae latinitatis ex florentissimo Ciceronis seculo petendae: neglandes frugibus praferantur.
main_text.head: Exercitatio II.

head.i:
Progymnasma in genere Demonstrativo
De obedientia Scholastica.

main_text.p: EXordium a praecepto Rhetorum: Interesse ubi quis quid laudet: Hypothesis fit Chria Socratis, laudare Atheniensem Athenis facile esse.
Transitio ad propositionem per applicatione: Sic te existimare, Scholasticae obedientiae laudes ad Scholas pertinere.
Propositio figuretur anthypophora: Videri quidem juventuti gravem: sed esse praecipuum & necessarium Scholarum nervum ac decus: suis decorandum laudibus ut ametur, &c.
Commendationis argumenta sumantur ex locis suasoriis:

page.notes: No marginal notes on this page. The page is a scan with its left edge and the neighbouring page's edge visible; these are not transcribed. The Roman numerals were copied as printed, with the spacing and form of the scan (e.g. "III", "IV") given as the standard Roman numeral. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. The line "ex locis suasoriis:" is read with some uncertainty for "locis" (scan shows a long-s-like form). The bottom-right word "I.Locus" is read as a catchword.
